newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Warring Tajiks in talks after rebels seize towns.
newsitem.headline: Warring Tajiks in talks after rebels seize towns.

text.p: Tajik government officials and Islamic opposition representatives held local ceasefire talks in the central city of Garm on Monday after rebels seized two towns in north-central Tajikistan this month.

Officials at the Tajik defence ministry and United Nations observers monitoring a fragile nationwide ceasefire said the opposition now fully controlled Tajikabad, 245 km (150 miles) northeast of Dushanbe, after letting a last besieged unit of government troops withdraw from the town's airport.
On September 6, the opposition seized Dzhirgatal, some 35 km (20 miles), further to the northeast.
Talks in Garm began on Sunday but the first word on substantive negotiations was not expected until late on Monday.
Government officials in the capital Dushanbe said they expected the opposition to demand a full troop withdrawal from the Karategin valley. The authorities were unlikely to consent.
The U.N. called the rebel seizure of Dzhirgatal a breach of a September 1994 ceasefire, which was extended in July.

The rebels, who have waged a guerrilla war against the Dushanbe authorities since their defeat in a 1992 civil war, said they were responding to the government seizure of the strategic town of Tavildara.

Tavildara, 200 km (120 miles) east of Dushanbe, controls the narrow neck of mountainous country that links the western and eastern halves of Tajikistan. It fell to the government after weeks of fighting. Tajikabad and Dzhirgatal lie in the northern part of this central neck.
Tens of thousands have died and many more have lost their homes in fighting which devastated the country after the former Soviet republic gained independence on September 9, 1991.
